liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (2 reviews): Contains a painful cut, yet the performance still keeps its power; A three-chord riff around 16:30 sounds like The Knack's My Sharona [6][12]
- **Hard to Handle** (1 review): Among the shortest versions anywhere, yet extremely intense [7]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): The jam keeps climbing in energy [7]
- **Uncle John's Jam/** (1 review): The short track within a middling Dark Star has a likely improvised riff that became Slipknot five years later [5]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Pigpen is likely on organ, with wailing drums, after The Other One [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **There's resonance at**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **The Star Spangled Banner**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [17]
- **The Merry Go Round Broke**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Spring Song Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Take Me Out To The**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Uncle John's Jam/**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-11-07.sbd.kaplan.21762.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 119 min; rated 3/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd1969-11-07.sbd.miller.119628.flac16**: soundboard; 16 songs; 145 min; rated 3.31/5 by 16 [2]
- **gd1969-11-07.sbd.cotsman.6299.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 102 min; rated 1.67/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: A repeated popping noise recurs through the recording; Faint popping, almost certainly from the reel recorder, runs through most of the recording and fades as reels run out [3][16]
- **gd69-11-07.sbd.kaplan.19783.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 119 min; rated 4.62/5 by 8 [4]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is great for its vintage, better than many old cassette copies; Board mix is essentially the same as 2-13-70, with slightly more audience, including screams and whistles [6][10]

## Around the show

- The tuning segments are audible on the recording, which reviewer enjoys [9]
- Wild audience screams can be heard on the 250 cycles track [9]
- The circulating tape cannot show whether the Dead played one set or two [1]
- Tunings of the national anthem, Merry-Go-Round Brokedown and the ballgame song come before Cold Rain [2]
- At the New Old Fillmore, other acts were South Bay Experimental Flash and Alligator [2]
- An unknown person plays The Star Spangled Banner on a pennywhistle [3]
- Deadbase places Hard To Handle and Casey Jones after Morning Dew, and High Time after Next Time You See Me [3]
- The 11/02/69 Family Dog Dark Star has a similar three-chord riff [12]
- Reviewer considers the following day's show among their absolute favorites [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-11-07.sbd.kaplan.21762.shnf**: transferred by Seth Kaplan; source: MR > DAT > CD > EAC > CDWAV > Cool Edit Pro Noise Filter > SHN > CDR (Except for * which is MR > DAT > CD) [1]. Also: Splices surround Mama Tried, Next Time You See Me and Good Lovin'; songs are probably missing [1]
- **gd1969-11-07.sbd.miller.119628.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat [2]. Also: Reel flips occur in High Time and the Uncle John's Band jam; there are no pauses, cuts or edits between songs [2]
- **gd1969-11-07.sbd.cotsman.6299.shnf**: taped by Paul Hartman; transferred by encoding/edits by J. Cotsman; source: SBD>MR>C>D>CD>EAC>SHN [3]
- **gd69-11-07.sbd.kaplan.19783.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Seth Kaplan; source: Soundboard [4]
